findings.description: The inline policy grants wildcard '*' actions on ec2, s3, lambda, and cloudwatch with Resource '*', violating least privilege and allowing the IAM user to perform virtually any action on these services, including privilege escalation and data exfiltration.

Creating a static IAM access key/secret for a user provides long-lived credentials that can be leaked or misused; combined with the overly permissive policy this significantly increases risk, and access keys are generally discouraged in favor of roles/temporary credentials.

findings.issue_category: standalone IAM user with excessive privileges
findings.description: An IAM user is created without any group-based or role-based access control, directly attached to an overly permissive inline policy, increasing the blast radius if the credentials are compromised.
